results.content:
In short, nearly every component in the automotive supply chain — from engines to electrical modules — can now face import duties depending on where it’s made and whether it qualifies for trade agreement exemptions.

## Auto Tariffs by Country: No Longer One Rate for All [...] Until early 2025, the United States applied a uniform 25% tariff on most imported automobiles, with a longstanding 2.5% base duty for passenger cars. But recent trade negotiations have reshaped the landscape. As of July 28, 2025, auto tariffs vary significantly by country, based on bilateral agreements or their absence.

Here’s a breakdown of where major U.S. trading partners currently stand: [...] Example: A Chinese brake rotor taxed at 25% steel tariff will not be taxed an additional 25% as an auto part

### 🛠️ Exceptions for Essential Replacement Parts

Select categories of parts used for maintenance and safety repairs may receive exemptions — especially:

 Brake systems
 Airbags
 Headlights and lighting modules

Exemptions are granted through a petition process and apply only to direct replacements for vehicles already on U.S. roads.

[...] The net result is a massive increase in tariffs for automotive goods imported into the United States, which will have a major impact on the entire automotive sector, which is an industry dependent on a complex international supply chain. To help automotive companies understand the impact of these tariffs, we are presenting a summary of the current status of the tariffs, as well as Frequently Asked Questions that we are receiving from various clients.

## Automotive Tariffs: What We Know So Far [...] IEEPA Global and Reciprocal Tariffs: The final set is the largest set of tariffs by far, which include (1) 10% global tariffs imposed on the entire world and (2) reciprocal tariffs, which are calculated based mostly on the level of the trade deficit with each country. The calculated ranges for these tariffs go from 10% (countries subject only to the global tariffs, like Singapore and the United Kingdom), up to 49%. ## Automotive News's post

### Automotive News

5 June  ·

Vehicles and parts already subject to auto tariffs would be exempt from new duties on 60 U.S. trading partners, the Trump administration proposed June 2.

The administration said it plans to place tariffs of 10 percent or 12.5 percent on countries including Canada, Mexico, Japan, South Korea, China and the United Kingdom, as well as the European Union.
